user.title: ClimateSync – Step 1 of 4: Heating sources
user.description: Select every room thermostat whose heating gap may control the destination. The **Heating Demand Active** entity uses all of these sources. A source must expose a current temperature and target temperature; an `off` source with a valid current temperature contributes zero demand.

primary_sources.title: ClimateSync – Step 2 of 4: Primary sources
primary_sources.description: Select the rooms that may enable other rooms to piggyback on an existing heating run. The **Primary Heating Demand Active** entity uses only this subset and the same hysteresis as general demand. A secondary source can still start general heating when it is below its own target, but it will not activate the primary-demand entity.

destination.title: ClimateSync – Step 3 of 4: Destination setpoint
destination.description: Select the thermostat ClimateSync controls and how the requested setpoint is formed. Choose **Target temperature** for ordinary climates or **Lower target temperature** for a heating-range climate; the current upper target is then preserved atomically. The idle temperature withdraws demand, while the maximum setpoint is a hard safety ceiling.

control.title: ClimateSync – Step 4 of 4: Demand & safeguards
control.description: The activation and deactivation thresholds form one hysteresis band for both demand entities: demand starts at the higher value and remains active until it reaches the lower value. **Minimum change** prevents insignificant destination writes; it does not decide whether demand is active. Resync recovers missed events and the minimum send interval rate-limits writes.

init.title: ClimateSync – Step 1 of 4: Heating sources
init.description: Select every room thermostat whose heating gap may control the destination. The **Heating Demand Active** entity uses all of these sources. Removing a source also removes it from the selectable primary subset.

primary_sources.title: ClimateSync – Step 2 of 4: Primary sources
primary_sources.description: Select the rooms that may enable other rooms to piggyback on an existing heating run. The **Primary Heating Demand Active** entity uses only this subset and the same hysteresis as general demand. Secondary sources still contribute to general demand but never to primary demand.

destination.title: ClimateSync – Step 3 of 4: Destination setpoint
destination.description: Choose the destination thermostat and setpoint behaviour. For a heating-range climate, select **Lower target temperature**; ClimateSync preserves the current upper target in the same action. Idle withdraws demand, and the maximum setpoint remains a hard ceiling.

Resync recovers missed events and the minimum send interval rate-limits writes.
